wheel.note: Factory torque not confirmed from a YJ owner's manual. Quadratec's generic chart gives 75–85 lb-ft for 1/2 in studs and says to check the owner's manual.

max_tire.note: Jeep's own Renegade size, so it fits an unmodified YJ; bigger tires on stock springs depend on wheel backspacing and flares.
Rough Country's 2.5 in YJ kit lists clearance for 31s on 15x8 wheels; test-fit the wheel and tire before you commit.
Rough Country's 4 in YJ kit lists 33x12.50 on 17-, 18- and 20-inch wheels; the 20-inch combos need minor trimming. Plan a re-gear from the factory ratio.

items.title: Windshield frame cracks at wiper pivots
items.summary: The frame can crack at the wiper-arm pivots; the fix was a reinforcement and redesigned wiper linkage. A follow-up campaign (93V150000) covered 1989 trucks.

items.title: Front brake hoses rub on splash shields
items.summary: Hoses can wear through on the wheel-opening splash shields; the fix was new shields or fasteners and new hoses where needed.

items.title: Fuel tank skid plate misbuilt
items.summary: In a rear impact the tank could leak more fuel than FMVSS 301 allows because of a misbuilt skid plate.

items.title: Starter can engage without the key
items.summary: Salt corrosion in the bulkhead connector can short the starter wire to battery feed; the fix relocates the wire in the connector.

items.title: Fuel sender gasket cracks
items.summary: On trucks with plastic tanks the sending-unit gasket can crack and leak fuel and vapor; the fix is a new gasket.

items.title: Parking brake can self-release (manual trans)
items.summary: Dealers fitted a parking-brake assembly with a stronger pawl return spring.

items.title: Front rotor corrosion (salt-belt states)
items.summary: For trucks sold or registered in listed salt-belt states, the stamped-steel rotor hub can rust through; replaced with coated rotors.

timeline.change: YJ launches (unveiled February 1986, on sale May 1986) with the 2.5 L four or carbureted 4.2 L six and the NP207 transfer case, used only this year
NP231 transfer case replaces the NP207; Sahara trim debuts; Islander package runs 1988–93
Aisin AX-15 five-speed replaces the Peugeot BA-10 behind the 4.2 L six
Fuel-injected 4.0 L six replaces the carbureted 4.2; Renegade Decor Group arrives (built from October 1990)
Brampton plant closes in April and production moves to Toledo; roll cage extended for rear shoulder belts; electronic speedometer
Automatic offered with the four; center high-mounted stop lamp; clutch slave cylinder moved outside the bellhousing for easier replacement
Larger Dana 30 U-joints (297x) and 1330 rear pinion joint; Rio Grande package; last YJs (there is no 1996 Wrangler)

identify.intro: Sixes, trim packages and build plant all change what a YJ is worth, and a lot of 30-year-old Jeeps have had engines, axles and decals swapped. Let the VIN and the hardware tell the story.

items.head: VIN, 1989–95
items.body: The 5th character is Y (Wrangler). The 6th is the trim: 4 is Sahara, 5 Laredo, 6 Renegade. The 8th is the engine: E is the 2.5 L four, S the 4.0 L six (1991–95), and M (1989) or T (1990) the 4.2 L six.

items.head: VIN, 1987–88
items.body: Early trucks use the older AMC-style VIN, starting 2BC on the Brampton-built examples we decoded. The 4th character is the engine (C is the 4.2 L six; H the 2.5 L TBI four) and characters 6–7 read 81 for Wrangler.

items.head: Brampton or Toledo
items.body: In the NHTSA decoder, VINs starting with 2 decode to Brampton, Ontario, and VINs starting with 1J4 to Toledo, Ohio. Brampton built YJs until April 1992.

items.head: Renegade
items.body: Real Renegades were finished by Autostyle near Detroit and carry a small Autostyle sticker on the driver's door jamb above the latch. They came with the 4.0 six, 8-inch alloys, 30x9.50 tires, fender-mounted fog lights and the 20-gallon tank.

items.head: Engine and transfer case
items.body: A 4.0 L six means 1991 or later; a 4.2 means 1990 or earlier. The NP207 transfer case is 1987 only; everything after uses the NP231.

items.head: Late YJ details
items.body: 1994–95 manual trucks have the external clutch slave cylinder. Some last-build 1995s got TJ-style hood bump stops, reinforced tailgate hinges and TJ rear bumpers.

values.intro: YJs are still the cheap way into a Wrangler, but nicer ones keep climbing. Low miles, the 4.0 six, a five-speed and Sahara, Renegade or Jurassic Park-style specs bring the money.
values.note: Based on 71 Bring a Trailer sales from January 2025 to October 2026: median ≈$9,800, middle half ≈$7,300–17,000. The top results were a 460-mile 1995 Sahara ($47,250, February 2025) and a 6k-mile 1995 Sahara ($49,750, September 2024).
